summary: The note surveys entrepreneurial and policy responses to textile waste in the US, covering recycling programs, circular fashion brands, consultancies, education, legislation, technology, and funding. It opens with the scale of the problem (about 80 pounds of textiles discarded per American yearly, over 11 million tons landfilled) and profiles individuals and initiatives working to turn waste into economic value. It closes with the role of financial support and international partnerships in making the shift financially viable and global.
one_line: Overview of entrepreneurs, policies, technologies, and funding turning textile waste into business opportunity through recycling and circular fashion.
key_facts: The average American discards approximately 80 pounds of textiles each year, and only a fraction is recycled.
As of October 15, 2023, more than 11 million tons of textile waste were destined for landfills in the United States.
Sarah Thompson, a former fashion merchandiser, launched the city-wide textile recycling initiative "ReFiber" on November 1, 2023, using a network of smart bins across urban spaces.

ReFiber's sorting facilities, operational since December 2023, sort textiles by fabric type and condition; good items go to thrift stores or global distribution, worn items become insulation, carpet padding, or industrial rags.
Carlos Fernandez launched the "Circular Threads" project on September 2, 2023, making garments from 100% recycled fabrics and offering lifetime repairs and a buy-back scheme.
Emily Huang launched the consultancy "GreenWeave Consulting" in January 2024, offering waste audits, supply chain analysis, and strategic recycling blueprints.
Educational consultant Michael Daniels launched the "Fashion's Footprint" campaign on September 10, 2023, creating school curricula on sustainable fashion.
Angela Richardson inaugurated the "Swap Till You Drop" clothing exchange fair on October 7, 2023.

Councilwoman Laura Gomez introduced a bill on November 20, 2023, offering tax incentives for sustainable practices and textile recycling, mandating clearer labeling, and making companies liable for end-of-life disposal of products once passed.
Dr. Helen Zhao's enzyme-based treatment research, concluding with a breakthrough in early 2024, separates blended fibers without degrading material quality.
Digital fashion and 3D software, increasingly adopted since late 2023, reduce the need for physical prototypes through precise measurements and virtual fittings.
The federal government initiated the "CleanTex Funding Program" in September 2024, offering grants and zero-interest loans to textile startups.
As of early 2025, international partnerships promoting technology transfer and shared expertise in textile recycling have become increasingly common.
